method: PyGhidra DecompInterface decompile of ui_welcome_animation (0x1ae9), creation_stage_dispatcher_by_step (0x15d7), ui_train_attribute_picker_grid (0x229c), wpcmk_train_skill_pillar (0x28d4), personality_roll_static_10_to_18 (0x4222), race_specific_init_handler_dispatch (0x48e3). Direct byte-pattern scan for writes to DGROUP 0x5588-0x558b (training points) and 0x5618 (skill_points). Jump table reconstruction using DELTA=0x4564 (wpcmk runtime delta: file_offset = CS_offset - 0x4564). Cross-referenced against msg-strings findings (wpcmk-msg-strings.json) and screen-flow findings (wpcmk-screen-flow.json).

screen_13_14_resolution.screen_13_actual: SKILL training (weapon skills, personal skills, physical skills, academic skills) — CONFIRMED BY ASM
screen_13_14_resolution.screen_14_actual: SPELL school selection (which spell school gets starter spell points: MAGIC/FAITH/PHYSICAL/MENTAL pillars) — CONFIRMED BY ASM
screen_13_14_resolution.explanation: The conflict arose from incorrect English labels in the prior screen-flow pass. ASM decompile definitively resolves it: (1) screen-13 driver is ui_welcome_animation (0x1ae9) calling creation_stage_dispatcher_by_step (0x15d7), which displays skill category headers from msg base 0x0258 (WEAPONRY=0x258, PHYSICAL=0x259, PERSONAL=0x25a, ACADEMIA=0x25b) and individual skill names from msg base 0x157c (WAND&DAGGER, SWORD, AXE, etc.) and 'SKILL POINTS' label (msg 0x159a). The loop drives *(char*)0x5618 to 0 = allocating skill points from a pool. (2) screen-14 driver is wpcmk_train_skill_pillar (0x28d4) which displays 'SPELLS' title (msg 0x2bc=700), 'SELECT A NEW SPELL FOR YOUR SPELLBOOK' (msg 0x2bf=703), 'COST' (msg 0x0f75=3957), spell school names FIRE/WATER/AIR/EARTH/MENTAL/MAGIC (msg base 0x0f6e), and individual spell names from msg base 0x0fa0 (ENERGY BLAST, FIREBALL, etc.), and decrements *(char*)(pillar+0x5588) after each pick. These are two completely different UI flows touching completely different data. Task 2 screen-flow labeled them backwards; Task 4 msg-strings correctly identified the string content. The msg-strings evidence was correct.

starter_pool.evidence: wpcmk file 0x4261 (inside personality_roll_static_10_to_18 at 0x4222): 'func_0x0000c47e(9)' = wroot rng thunk returning 0..8 (exclusive upper bound 9); result stored as '*(char*)0x5618 = rng_result + 10'. ASM: b8 09 00 50 e8 XX XX (push 9; call rng); 59 (pop); 80 c0 0a (add al, 10); a2 18 56 (mov [0x5618], al). This is NOT a fixed value of 10 — the min is 10 (when rng returns 0) and max is 18 (when rng returns 8).
starter_pool.per_class_variation: After personality_roll sets 0x5618 = rng(9)+10, each class-specific handler (dispatched via jump table at file 0x4545, runtime 0x8aa9) may subtract an attribute-derived 'tier2 adjustment' from 0x5618. The adjustment formula is: tier2 = (int)(attr_value / div) + base_increment, where div and base_increment differ per class. Classes that do NOT modify 0x5618 (they jump to epilog directly): Mage, Priest, Thief, Alchemist, Bard, Psionic, Valkyrie, Lord, Samurai. Classes that subtract a computed tier2: Fighter, Ranger, Bishop, Monk, Ninja. The tier2 subtraction pattern: 'a0 18 56; 2a e4; 2b 46 f4; a2 18 56' = load skill_pts, clear AH, subtract [bp-0xc] (tier2), store back. If skill_pts <= tier2: store 0 instead (Fighter special case at 0x4580: c6 06 18 56 00).
starter_pool.note: The existing viewer placeholder of 10 is the MINIMUM possible value (when rng returns 0). Most characters will have 11..18 skill points. A correct implementation should use rng(9)+10.

pillar_mapping.what_is_trained: MAGIC spell schools — player selects from grid which magic spell school gets initial spell points (e.g. FIRE, WATER, AIR, EARTH, MENTAL, MAGIC categories in ui_train_attribute_picker_grid)
FAITH spell schools — divine/priestly spell schools
PHYSICAL spell schools — alchemical/physical magic schools
MENTAL spell schools — psionic/mental magic schools

per_class_training_pts.evidence: Jump table at wpcmk file 0x4a6d (runtime 0x8fd1) dispatched by race_specific_init_handler_dispatch (0x48e3). Each class handler scanned for 'c6 06 XX 55 YY' = mov byte [0x55XX], YY patterns where XX in {88,89,8a,8b}. Verified: Mage handler at file 0x492d writes c6 06 88 55 02; Priest at 0x4952 writes c6 06 89 55 02; Alchemist at 0x498f writes c6 06 8a 55 02; Psionic at 0x49cc writes c6 06 8b 55 02; Bishop at 0x4a03 writes c6 06 88 55 01 followed by c6 06 89 55 01. All other classes land at handlers with no 0x5588-0x558b writes.

findings.claim: Screen-13 (ui_welcome_animation at 0x1ae9 / creation_stage_dispatcher_by_step at 0x15d7) is the SKILL training screen, NOT the spell school animation. It shows weapon skill categories (WEAPONRY/PHYSICAL/PERSONAL/ACADEMIA) and individual skill names (WAND&DAGGER, SWORD, AXE, etc.) from the skill table. The player allocates skill points from a pool of rng(9)+10 = 10..18.

evidence.details: ui_welcome_animation (0x1ae9): calls creation_stage_dispatcher_by_step in loop while *(char*)0x5618 != 0. msg-strings scan found: creation_stage_dispatcher_by_step at 0x1941 writes msg_id = arg + 0x0258 (WEAPONRY/PHYSICAL/PERSONAL/ACADEMIA/EXIT/YOU EARNED A SKILL BONUS), at 0x1a34 writes msg_id = arg + 0x157c (WAND&DAGGER/SWORD/AXE/MACE&FLAIL/...), at 0x1aa5 writes msg 0x159a = 'SKILL POINTS'. These are weapon/personal/academic skill names, not spell names.

findings.claim: Screen-14 (wpcmk_train_skill_pillar at 0x28d4 / ui_train_attribute_picker_grid at 0x229c) is the SPELL school selection screen, NOT generic skill training. It shows a 6-cell grid of spell schools (FIRE/WATER/AIR/EARTH/MENTAL/MAGIC) and individual spell names (ENERGY BLAST, FIREBALL, etc.). Only Mage, Priest, Alchemist, Psionic, and Bishop get this screen; all other classes have 0 training points and skip it entirely.

evidence.details: wpcmk_train_skill_pillar (0x28d4) decompile: param_3 maps to pillar mask (0→8=MAGIC, 1→4=FAITH, 2→1=PHYSICAL, 3→2=MENTAL). At 0x29fd: calls func_0x0000c2db(0x2bf, ...) where 0x2bf = msg 703 = 'SELECT A NEW SPELL FOR YOUR SPELLBOOK'. At 0x1d93 (ui_draw_train_screen_borders): calls c2db(0x2bc) = msg 700 = 'SPELLS'. At 0x2424: calls c2db(0x0f74) = msg 3956 = 'CANCEL'. At 0x224c (ui_render_skill_grid_entry): ax = [bx] + 0x0fa0 (spell names base). The 'skill' being trained is a SPELL SCHOOL entry from the wroot DGROUP spell table, not the weapon/personal skill table.

findings.claim: The spell training screen (screen-14) is completely skipped for Fighter, Thief, Ranger, Bard, Valkyrie, Lord, Samurai, Monk, and Ninja because all 4 pillar training point counters (0x5588-0x558b) are 0 for these classes. Only Mage (MAGIC=2), Priest (FAITH=2), Alchemist (PHYSICAL=2), Psionic (MENTAL=2), and Bishop (MAGIC=1, FAITH=1) get any spell training screen(s).

evidence.details: wpcmk_create_character_master inner loop: 'local_4 = 0; do { while (*(char*)(local_4+0x5588) != 0) { wpcmk_train_skill_pillar(win, charptr, local_4); } local_4++; } while (local_4 < 4)'. Race_specific_init_handler_dispatch jump table at file 0x4a6d (runtime 0x8fd1). Only 5 of 14 class handlers write to 0x5588-0x558b. Verified by scanning all 14 handlers.

findings.claim: The starter SKILL points pool for screen-13 is rng(9)+10 = 10..18, NOT a fixed value of 10. Stored at DGROUP 0x5618. The existing viewer placeholder of 10 is only the minimum possible value.

evidence.details: personality_roll_static_10_to_18 at 0x4222: push 9; call rng_thunk(0xc47e); pop; add al, 10; mov [0x5618], al. This sets skill_pts = rng(0..8) + 10. Then dispatches via class jump table at file 0x4545 (runtime 0x8aa9) where class-specific handlers may subtract an attribute-derived 'tier2' adjustment. Classes that don't modify the pool keep the full rng(9)+10 value. Fighter gets a special capped subtraction (result = max(0, skill_pts - tier2)).

findings.claim: The 82-entry skill table accessed by wpcmk_train_skill_pillar at DGROUP addresses 0xde..0x322 is NOT in wpcmk.ovr — it lives in wroot's DGROUP BSS at runtime. wpcmk accesses it via the shared DGROUP segment. Each 6-byte entry: byte+0 = governing_attr (0..5 = STR/INT/PIE/VIT/DEX/SPD), byte+1 = min_level, byte+2 = max_level, ..., byte+5 = pillar_mask (bitfield: 8=MAGIC, 4=FAITH, 1=PHYSICAL, 2=MENTAL). The decompile expression '*(byte*)(local_4*6 + 0xe3)' accesses byte+5 (pillar_mask) of entry local_4.

evidence.details: wpcmk_train_skill_pillar loop: 'if ((local_c & *(byte*)((int)local_4*6 + 0xe3)) != 0) && ((int)(uint)*(byte*)((int)local_4*6+0xdf) <= local_a)' — local_c is the pillar bitmask, 0xe3 is the mask byte offset, 0xdf is the min_level byte offset. These are wroot DGROUP runtime addresses (verified: 0xde-0x322 = 82 * 6 = 492 bytes, matches 82-entry count). The base for entry N is 0xde + N*6; fields are at offsets +0(governing_attr), +1(min_level), +2(max_level), +5(pillar_mask).

findings.claim: ui_welcome_animation (0x1ae9) is the outer shell for screen-13 (skill training). It creates a new window (ui_window_create thunk 0xbbb6 with size 20x4x20x16x25), then loops: (1) call creation_stage_dispatcher_by_step(window, param_1, step_counter), (2) call ui_class_menu_with_qualification(param_1, window), (3) advance step_counter mod 4 (skipping step 2 when dispatcher returns 0). Loop exits when *(char*)0x5618 == 0.

evidence.details: Decompile: 'local_6 = func_0x0000bbb6(0x14,4,0x14,0x10,0x19,0xffff,0,0)' (create window 20 cols, 4 rows, at pos 20,16 with height 25); 'local_4 = 0x11; do { local_4++; } while (local_4 < 0x16)' (initialization loop 0x12..0x15 = 4 iters); then main loop: 'local_1c[0] = creation_stage_dispatcher_by_step(local_6, param_1, iVar2); ui_class_menu_with_qualification(param_1, local_6); iVar2 = ((int)ppppuVar3 + 1) % 4; if (iVar2==2 && ppppuVar1==0) iVar2=3; while (*(char*)0x5618 != 0)'. The step counter iVar2 cycles 0→1→2→3→0... skipping step 2 when the dispatcher returns 0.

findings.claim: ui_train_attribute_picker_grid (0x229c) shows a 6-cell grid (2 rows × 3 cols) of spell schools. Key 1/2/3/4 navigate up/left/down/right; key 5 selects. After cell selection, shows a scrollable list of spells for that school. Key 2/4 scroll the list up/down; key 1 cancels; key 5 confirms. Returns the selected spell index or -1 on cancel (CANCEL button). The 6 cells display spell school names from msg base 0x0f6e: FIRE(0)/WATER(1)/AIR(2)/EARTH(3)/MENTAL(4)/MAGIC(5).

evidence.details: Decompile shows: two windows created (local_4=outer frame, local_6=spell list panel). Grid navigation: key1→uVar4-=3 (up), key2→uVar4-=1 (left), key3→uVar4+=3 (down clamp to 0xffff=cancel), key4→uVar4+=1 (right). After cell pick: skill_find_indices_by_attr (not named yet) fills local_34[]; ui_render_skill_grid_entry renders each spell; key2→local_3c-- (scroll up), key4→local_3c++ (scroll down), key5→return local_34[local_3c] (return spell index), key1→iVar1=1 (cancel flag). Returns -1 if CANCEL cell (uVar4==0xffff) is confirmed. Spell display check: 'if *(int*)(uVar4*4+0x5498) < (int)(uint)*(byte*)(local_34[local_3c]*6+0xe0)' — cost check against current attr pool.

findings.claim: When a spell is selected in wpcmk_train_skill_pillar, the spell's governing attribute pools at DGROUP 0x5498 (cur) and 0x549a (max) are incremented. The increment amount is bounded by the spell's max value at skill_table[skill_idx].byte2 (0xe0). Formula: delta = min(skill_entry.min_level_attr_pts * 2 + 1, skill_entry.max_val - current_pool). After update, the pillar counter *(char*)(param_3+0x5588) is decremented by 1.

evidence.details: After ui_train_attribute_picker_grid returns local_8 (skill index): 'iVar1 = local_8*6; local_4 = (uint)*(byte*)(iVar1+0xdf)*2 + 1' (delta = min_level_pts*2+1); 'local_6 = (uint)*(byte*)(iVar1+0xde)' (governing_attr); 'iVar2 = local_6*4'; 'if (*(int*)(iVar2+0x549a) + local_4 < (uint)*(byte*)(iVar1+0xe0)) { local_4 stays }; else { local_4 = *(byte*)(iVar1+0xe0) - *(int*)(iVar2+0x549a) }'; '*(int*)(iVar2+0x549a) += local_4; *(int*)(iVar2+0x5498) += local_4; *(char*)(param_3+0x5588) -= 1'.

findings.claim: skill_init_all_32_slots (0x392e) calls FUN_38fb(idx, 9) for 32 skill slots (indices 0..31). FUN_38fb (0x38fb) writes to DGROUP 0x55d8+idx: 'value = (KAR - 9 == 0) ? 0 : abs(KAR - 9); slot_speed = -4 * value + 40'. This initializes per-skill speed modifiers based on the karma stat. The formula gives slot_speed in {-152..40} (KAR range 10..18 → |KAR-9| = 1..9 → slot_speed = 36..4). NOT a skill pool init.

evidence.details: FUN_38fb(param_1, param_2=9): 'if (*(byte*)0x55a3 < param_2) cVar1 = -(*(byte*)0x55a3 - param_2); else cVar1 = *(char*)0x55a3 - param_2; *(char*)(param_1+0x55d8) = cVar1 * -4 + 40'. So slot_speed[idx] = -4 * |KAR - 9| + 40. Range: KAR=10: -4*1+40=36; KAR=18: -4*9+40=4. Called for idx 0..9, 11..31 (32 calls; idx 10 is absent from skill_init_all_32_slots but this is a Ghidra decompile artifact — the original asm likely has idx=10 too).

state_machine.description: Screen-13 (skill training) has an implicit loop driven by 0x5618 > 0. Screen-14 (spell training) has an implicit loop driven by any pillar 0x5588-0x558b > 0. Both are inside wpcmk_create_character_master's outer flow.

states.description: creation_stage_dispatcher_by_step showing skill category header (WEAPONRY/PHYSICAL/PERSONAL/ACADEMIA). Tracks step_counter (0..3 cycling mod 4).
Within a category: scrollable list of individual skill names. Player picks a skill, skill points are consumed.
wpcmk_train_skill_pillar showing 6-cell spell-school grid. Active for pillars 0-3 where *(0x5588+pillar) > 0.
After selecting a spell school cell: scrollable spell list for that school.
states.trigger: Player selects a spell-school cell in the 6-cell grid

transitions.condition: Player selects a category (key 5 on a non-EXIT entry)
Player picks a skill (key 5) → 0x5618 decremented. If 0x5618 > 0 still, loops back to category.
*(char*)0x5618 becomes 0 → ui_welcome_animation exits → master loop proceeds to wpcmk_train_skill_pillar
Player picks a spell (key 5 non-cancel) → *(0x5588+pillar) decremented. Loop continues if > 0.
*(0x5588+pillar) hits 0 → advance to next pillar (local_4++) up to 4

key_handlers.action: Move selection up (uVar4 -= 3, wraps to cancel=0xffff if uVar4 < 2)
Move selection left (uVar4 -= 1, only if uVar4 % 3 > 0)
Move selection down (uVar4 += 3, clamp to 0xffff=CANCEL if > 5)
Move selection right (uVar4 += 1, only if uVar4 % 3 < 2)
Confirm selection. If uVar4==0xffff (CANCEL cell): return -1. Else: enter spell-list sub-picker for that school.
Cancel and return to spell school grid (iVar1=1 flag → break inner loop)
Scroll spell list down (local_3c++ if < local_c-1)
Select currently highlighted spell (return local_34[local_3c] = skill table index)
Dispatches via jump table at file 0x6d9c (runtime). Direct click on a cell selects or navigates it.

dgroup_addresses.skill_points_remaining_screen13: 0x5618 (byte) — initialized by personality_roll_static_10_to_18 to rng(9)+10; decremented by ui_class_menu_with_qualification after each skill pick; loop in ui_welcome_animation exits when 0
dgroup_addresses.spell_train_pts_pillar0_MAGIC: 0x5588 (byte) — count of spell picks remaining for MAGIC pillar; decremented by wpcmk_train_skill_pillar after each pick
dgroup_addresses.spell_attr_pool_cur_base: 0x5498 (int[6]) — cur spell points per governing attr (0..5 = STR/INT/PIE/VIT/DEX/SPD), stride 4: *(0x5498 + attr*4)
dgroup_addresses.spell_attr_pool_max_base: 0x549a (int[6]) — max spell points per governing attr, stride 4: *(0x549a + attr*4)

skill_table_structure.description: 82-entry spell/skill table in wroot DGROUP. Accessed by wpcmk_train_skill_pillar for spell training (screen-14). Entry N starts at DGROUP 0xde + N*6.

field_offsets.byte+0: governing_attr — index 0..5 = STR/INT/PIE/VIT/DEX/SPD; controls which 0x5498+attr*4 pool gets updated
field_offsets.byte+1: min_level — minimum character level to pick this entry (always 1 for new char creation)
field_offsets.byte+2: max_val — max value cap for the governing attribute pool (used in increment formula)
field_offsets.byte+5: pillar_mask — bitmask: 8=MAGIC, 4=FAITH, 1=PHYSICAL, 2=MENTAL; a single entry can appear in multiple pillars

skill_table_structure.decompile_refs: wpcmk_train_skill_pillar at 0x28d4: '*(byte*)(local_4*6 + 0xe3)' = entry[N].byte5 = pillar_mask; '*(byte*)(local_4*6 + 0xdf)' = entry[N].byte1 = min_level; '*(byte*)(local_8*6 + 0xde)' = entry[chosen].byte0 = governing_attr; '*(byte*)(local_8*6 + 0xe0)' = entry[chosen].byte2 = max_val

open_questions: The class-specific tier2 adjustment to skill_pts (subtracting from 0x5618) in the handlers at 0x426b-0x456d is not fully decoded. The formula involves attribute-derived arithmetic (INT/PIE/VIT/SPD divisions). A complete class-by-class table of expected skill-pts ranges after tier2 adjustment would require tracing each handler's attribute reads. Priority: medium (affects starting skill points for Fighter/Ranger/Bishop/Monk/Ninja).

The 82-entry skill table at wroot DGROUP 0xde..0x322 was not fully decoded in this pass. Only the field layout (6 bytes per entry: governing_attr, min_level, max_val, ..., pillar_mask) is confirmed from the access patterns in wpcmk_train_skill_pillar. The full table data (which skills map to which pillars, which attrs govern them) requires reading from a live save-state via dosbox_read_memory at DGROUP offset 0xde.

The class_skill_init jump table handlers (at file 0x426b-0x456d) also write to other DGROUP addresses (0x55af, 0x55be, 0x55c0, 0x55ad, etc.) that were not decoded. These may be additional class-specific stats. They are NOT 0x5588-0x558b (training points). Possibly spell school capacity or category enablement flags.

ui_class_menu_with_qualification (0x1158) writes '*(undefined1*)0x5618 = local_1c' (line 409 of decompile). The value local_1c is the return value (number of skills available in the selected category? remaining skill points?). This write is the skill_pts decrement from screen-13. The exact decrement logic (does it decrement by 1 per pick or by the number of skills in a category?) needs verification.

The 'skill_find_indices_by_attr' call inside ui_train_attribute_picker_grid fills local_34[] with spell indices for the selected school and returns local_c (count). This function was not independently decompiled. Its name is inferred from context. File offset not determined in this pass.

The mouse jump table at file 0x6d9c (runtime, accessed via ui_train_attribute_picker_grid's mouse handler) was not decoded. Mouse button → key mapping is partially documented (button0..9 dispatched via table), but exact mapping is unknown.

Bishop's spell training: MAGIC=1 and FAITH=1. The master loop runs wpcmk_train_skill_pillar for pillar 0 (MAGIC) first, then pillar 1 (FAITH). So Bishop gets 2 separate spell-pick screens in sequence. This is the expected behavior but should be verified against a live Bishop character creation in DOSBox-X.

The 'while (*(char*)(local_4+0x5588) != 0)' inner loop in wpcmk_create_character_master means if a class had training_pts > 1 for a pillar (none do in the current data, max is 2), that pillar would show multiple picks. Mage has MAGIC=2 which means Mage gets 2 separate MAGIC spell picks. The loop structure: 'while pts>0: call wpcmk_train_skill_pillar(pillar); pts decremented inside the pillar fn; re-check'.
